..
Issued at 256 AM EDT Thu Oct 15 2026

Today-Friday...Broad area of high pressure north of the area will 
gradually shift eastward as a mid/upper level trough moving into the 
Central U.S. pushes a cold front into the southeast states. Onshore 
winds will continue across the area, but will weaken into tomorrow, 
with easterly winds increasing to around 10 mph this afternoon and 
then dropping to 5-10 mph on Friday. The onshore flow at the 
surface combined with S/SE winds aloft on the western edge of a 
mid level ridge transports deeper moisture northward across the 
area through late week, leading to rising rain chances across the 
area.

For today, rain chances (20-50%) remain mostly south of a line from 
Orlando to the Cape, where greatest moisture (PW values of 1.7-2.0") 
will reside. Isolated onshore moving showers will be possible along 
the coast, mainly south of the Cape this morning, and then isolated 
to scattered showers and a few storms are forecast to develop south 
of Orlando into this afternoon. Into Friday, PW values of 1.9-2.1" 
overspread all of east central Florida, with coverage of showers and 
storms increasing (PoPs 50-60%), becoming scattered to numerous 
primarily into the afternoon and early evening hours. Main storm 
threats each day will be occasional to frequent cloud to ground 
lightning, gusty winds up to 45 mph and locally heavy rainfall up
to 1-3". Temperatures climb to slightly above normal, with highs 
in the upper 80s to low 90s, and overnight lows in the low to mid 
70s.

Saturday-Wednesday...Weather conditions rapidly deteriorate into the 
weekend as trough aloft shifts into the eastern U.S. and pushes 
front through the area. Breezy to windy conditions quickly develop 
into Saturday as northerly winds increase to 15-25 mph, with gusts 
up to 30-40 mph (strongest along the coast). Wind Advisories will 
likely be needed for the coast into Saturday/Saturday night, and may 
even expand across inland areas during the day Sunday as northeast 
winds look to strengthen from tightening pressure gradient between 
front to the south and strong ridge to the north. Some forecast 
uncertainty does come into play later in the weekend into next week, 
as models show a cut-off low forming from the advancing trough and 
developing a strong area of low pressure at the surface either near 
(ECMWF) or well offshore (GFS) the Mid-Atlantic coast. Exact 
timing/location of this developing feature could lead to some 
differences in wind direction and overall speed. However, current 
forecast leans toward the GFS, which has more model support 
currently, maintaining breezy to windy NE winds through at least 
early next week. 

Models now show advancing front will push out some of the deeper 
moisture across the area, even as winds quickly veer onshore. Rain 
chances remain high up to 50-70% for much of the area Saturday. 
However, the GFS now has PW values falling below 1.5" by Sunday. 
Still, the strong onshore winds will still produce rounds of 
scattered to numerous showers that will be able to push onshore 
through late weekend into early next week. A few storms will also 
continue to be possible, mainly south of the Cape where some 
lingering instability will persist. Persistent bands of showers and 
any storms could lead to locally heavy to excessive rainfall, 
producing flooding issues, mainly across the Treasure Coast. A 
Marginal Risk for excessive rainfall (Level 1 of 4) exists across 
this portion of east central FL into the weekend. 

Cooler temperatures move in behind the front, with highs dropping to 
as low as the mid 70 to low 80s Sunday, and then slowly warming but 
remaining near to below normal through the middle of next week. The 
strong onshore winds will lead to a prolonged period of dangerous 
beach and boating conditions. High surf, with breaking waves of 9-12 
ft over multiple tidal cycles will contribute to moderate beach 
erosion, especially north of Cape Canaveral. Residents and visitors 
should use caution near the beach and remain out of the water.
